_meta.source: 16-agent evidence-based reconciliation: engine trees vs OSAP scripts, cell-level proofs
_meta.purpose: per-factor fix list for the correctness reconciliation (task #10 extended)

factors.evidence: Script Accruals.py L90-99 subtracts depreciation: (...) - df['dp'], then / ((at+lag_at)/2). Engine tree (p1_factor_specs.py) has only DELTA(act)-DELTA(che)-(DELTA(lct)-DELTA(dlc)-DELTA(fillna(txp,0))) over avg assets - NO dp term. Sampled IBM (12490) 1990-01: engine=0.059696 == no-dp formula 0.059696; oracle=0.003072 == with-dp formula 0.003072 (dp=3871); 1990-06: engine=-0.014791 vs oracle=-0.071035, again exactly matching no-dp vs with-dp. This mis-formula explains 2.98M/3.18M divergent cells. Secondary: 15,359 missing-in-engine cells come from the script's POSITION-based groupby(permno).shift(12) over gappy m_aCompustat rows: cell (permno 28388, 1966-06) oracle=-0.0031411229 exactly reproduced by the positional lag that lands on 1965-01 (17 calendar months back); engine's calendar 12-month wide-grid lag is NaN there.
factors.proposed_fix: Corrected tree: DIV( SUB( SUB( SUB(DELTA(act,12), DELTA(che,12)), SUB(SUB(DELTA(lct,12), DELTA(dlc,12)), DELTA(FILLNA(txp,0),12)) ), VAR(m_aCompustat.dp) ), DIV(ADD(at, LAG(at,12)), 2) ). I.e. add the missing SUB(..., dp) around the working-capital term. The positional-vs-calendar lag residual (15k cells, oracle uses stale >12mo-old data across Compustat gaps) is an oracle artifact of position shift; accept as known mask or demote if exact parity is required.

factors.evidence: Engine tree = LOG(DIV(m_aCompustat.at, m_aCompustat.ceq)). Script BookLeverage.py L72-97: txditc.fillna(0); tempPS=pstk->pstkrv->pstkl; tempSE=seq->(ceq+tempPS)->(at-lt); BookLeverage = at/(tempSE+txditc-tempPS) with be==0 -> NaN, and NO log despite the FF1992 'Ln(A/BE)' comment. Sampled IBM 1990-01: engine=0.614438 == log(at/ceq)=log(1.848617); oracle=1.654967 == at/BE. All 3,319,674 both-valued cells diverge. Misses (201,033): sample of 3000 -> 1192 have ceq NaN but script fallback computes via seq or at-lt (e.g. permno 22779 1951-06: seq/ceq NaN, oracle=54.8/(54.8-28.225)=2.0620885), 1808 have at/ceq<=0 so engine log() is NaN while script keeps the negative ratio. Extras (446, max_abs=Infinity): e.g. permno 27975 1973-07 ceq=0 -> engine log(at/0)=inf; script be==0 guard -> NaN.
factors.proposed_fix: Drop LOG entirely and rebuild denominator with fallbacks: PS = COALESCE(pstk, pstkrv, pstkl); SE = COALESCE(seq, ADD(ceq, PS), SUB(at, lt)); BookLeverage = DIV(at, ZERO_TO_NULL(SUB(ADD(SE, FILLNA(txditc,0)), PS))). Note NaN propagation must match the script: PS NaN makes the ceq+PS branch and the final be NaN even when SE came from seq (COALESCE(seq,...) then SUB(...,PS) reproduces this).

factors.evidence: Script AnalystRevision.py L43 restricts IBES to fpi=='1' before the ratio meanest/lag1(meanest). Engine tree is DIV(meanest, LAG(meanest,1)) on the generic var panel, and DatasetStore.get for LINKED_TICKER_MONTHLY_DATASETS (p1_factor_engine.py L416-431) pivots IBES_EPS_Unadj with NO fpi filter and aggfunc='last' - the last row per ticker-month is the fpi='6' (quarterly) row. Sampled IBM/tick BELW->IBM 1994-05: file rows are fpi0=9.00, fpi1=2.94, fpi2=4.44, fpi6=0.69; engine=6.900000 == 0.69/0.10 (fpi6 ratio), oracle=1.330317 == 2.94/2.21 (fpi1 ratio); every sampled month matches this pattern (engine col 'lastany_ratio' == engine output exactly). Explains 1.28M/1.91M divergent cells and max_abs=Infinity (fpi6 meanest hits 0). Extras (224,519): 967/1000 sampled extra cells are permno-months absent from SignalMasterTable (unfiltered CRSP universe + link-table join). Misses (9,701): script positional shift(1) over SMT gaps vs engine calendar lag.
factors.proposed_fix: Add a row-filter to the var node: VAR(IBES_EPS_Unadj, meanest, filter: fpi=='1') - or equivalently make the DatasetStore linked-ticker loader accept per-spec predicates and register IBES_EPS_Unadj.meanest with fpi=='1' for this factor. Keep the DIV/LAG(1) tree. Then mask output to the SignalMasterTable universe to remove the extra cells.

factors.evidence: Script BM.py L51-62: me_datadate = mve_permco.shift(6) kept ONLY where the 6-back month equals the datadate month, then unlimited groupby(permno).ffill() - market equity is FROZEN at fiscal-year-end and carried forward. Engine op _op_market_equity_matched_to_datadate (p1_factor_engine.py L762-766) literally does `_ = datadate; return _op_lag(x, 6)` - a plain rolling 6-month lag. Sampled IBM 1990: oracle constant -0.620748 Jan-May (frozen Dec-1988 FYE me), updating to -0.357246 at 1990-06; engine changes EVERY month (-0.558646, -0.576956, -0.488585, ...) and equals log(ceqt/mve_crsp_lag6) exactly each month; engine==oracle only in June when lag6 happens to land on the datadate month. Explains 2.45M/2.71M divergent cells. Extras (350,559): engine emits values for any month with ceqt & lag6-mve on the unfiltered CRSP grid, while oracle requires a prior successful datadate match within the SMT (right-join) universe.
factors.proposed_fix: Implement the op's declared semantics: me = LAG(mve_permco, 6); me = me.where(month(t-6) == month(datadate at t)); me = ffill(me) per permno (unlimited); BM = LOG(DIV(ceqt, me)). Use SMT mve_permco/universe (sampled values match monthlyCRSP mve_permco for IBM, so the source panel is fine; the mask to SMT rows removes extras). Caveat: the script's shift(6) is positional over SMT rows, so firms with listing gaps mis-match in the oracle - residual cells after the fix are oracle artifacts of position shift.

factors.evidence: Engine _prepare_analyst_value_signals (p1_factor_engine.py L1372-1386) builds its June panel as IBESCRSPLinkingTable INNER-merged with monthlyCRSP and m_aCompustat, then l12_ceq = groupby(permno).shift(1) over those June rows; the script (ZZ1 L91-142,156-172) uses the FULL SignalMasterTable June panel (left joins), so shift(1) always reaches the true previous June. Where a permno's first (or a gap) year in the link table, engine ceq_ave collapses to ceq instead of (ceq+prior_ceq)/2. Proven for permno 17559 (in link table only from 1984; SMT June rows from 1981): June-1984 engine golden 0.65401775 == recomputation with ceq_ave=ceq=6.777; oracle 0.6589706 == recomputation with ceq_ave=(6.777+6.055)/2=6.416 (exact to 7 digits). Whole first-IBES-year cohort diverges: all 441 divergent permnos at 1976-06..1977-05, then ~21/yr (link-table entry/gap years, e.g. 17559 again at 1995 after its 1994 link gap). 23,499 of the 23,667 divergent AOP cells are the same cells divergent in AnalystValue (shared ceq_ave). Extras (95,430): 1493/1500 sampled extra cells are permno-months not in SignalMasterTable.
factors.proposed_fix: In _prepare_analyst_value_signals, build the June base panel from the full CRSP/SMT permno-June universe (left-join the IBES link/estimates and Compustat like the script) so l12_ceq=shift(1) lands on the true prior June; equivalently compute l12_ceq as the calendar 12-month lag of June ceq from m_aCompustat independent of IBES coverage. Then mask final output to the SMT universe to remove extras.

factors.evidence: Shares _prepare_analyst_value_signals with AnalystValue - identical root cause. Same sampled proof, permno 17559 June-1984: engine AOP golden matches recomputation with ceq_ave=ceq (AOP=0.2165258), oracle matches ceq_ave=(ceq+prior_June_ceq)/2 (AOP=0.1483313); AOP is more sensitive than AnalystValue because ceq_ave drives ROE=ibcom/ceq_ave which enters IntrinsicValue (AOP denominator), hence max_abs=2399.8 when IntrinsicValue is near zero. 23,499 of 23,667 divergent cells coincide with AnalystValue's divergent cells; extra=95,430 cells are the same non-SMT universe cells (99.5% of sampled extras absent from SignalMasterTable).
factors.proposed_fix: Same fix as AnalystValue (one shared helper): June base panel from full SMT/CRSP June rows with left-joined IBES so l12_ceq/ceq_ave match the script, plus SMT universe mask on output. No tree change needed beyond the helper.

factors.evidence: (1) Value divergence (327,285 cells, constant within 12-month blocks = annual residual level): engine _trim_by_group (p1_factor_engine.py L1258-1272) trims temp vars at 0.1/99.9% using pandas quantile (linear interpolation); script winsor2 polars path (winsor2.py L128-152) uses polars .quantile() whose default interpolation is 'nearest' -> different trim thresholds -> different regression samples -> whole (fyear,sic2) group's residuals shift. Proven exactly for IBM (12490), fyear 1971, sic2=73: rebuilt regression with linear-interp trim gives residual -0.04706907 (44 obs) == engine golden -0.047069; nearest-interp trim gives -0.02899945 (45 obs) == oracle -0.028999. (2) Misses (123,740): script expands via fill_date_gaps_pl + UNLIMITED forward-fill to 12mo past the LAST annual obs (ZZ2 L215-229), carrying stale residuals through null-residual years - permno 58413's oracle holds -0.11658 continuously from 1986-06 to 2024-12 (38 years) while engine's _expand_hold_months(12)+dropna (L1703-1704) goes NaN after 1986-05; 1244/2000 sampled miss cells are >=12 months after the engine's last value. (3) Extras (11,601): engine takes exchcd from unfiltered monthlyCRSP (L1666-1671) with pandas boolean semantics, script left-joins SMT exchcd and polars filter(~((exchcd==3)&(fyear<1982))) DROPS null-exchcd rows pre-1982 (Kleene null); permno 58413 1977-06: monthlyCRSP exchcd=2.0, SMT row absent -> engine valued 1977-1981, oracle NaN.
factors.proposed_fix: Three changes in _op_abnormal_accruals_signal: (a) trim with interpolation='nearest' quantiles in _trim_by_group (or replicate polars quantile) - fixes the bulk value divergence; (b) replace _expand_hold_months(...,12)+dropna with the script's fill semantics: per-permno monthly backbone from first to last annual time_avail_m +12mo padding, forward-fill AbnormalAccruals without limit (do NOT drop null-residual annual rows before filling); (c) source exchcd from SignalMasterTable and drop rows where exchcd is null AND fyear<1982 to mirror polars Kleene filtering. Note (b) reproduces an oracle quirk (decades-stale values) - if undesired, flag as oracle_artifact instead and keep the 12-month hold deliberately.

factors.evidence: Engine custom op _op_brand_invest_signal (p1_factor_engine.py L1548-1600) seeds BrandCapital[first_pos]=xad/0.6 and starts the recursion at first_pos+1, preserving the seed. Oracle script BrandInvest.py L104-112 runs the recursion 'for i in range(1, len(gvkey_data))' unconditionally, so when the first non-missing xad is NOT the gvkey's first row (rows before it are seeded 0, L91), the xad/0.6 seed is OVERWRITTEN by 0.5*0+tempxad = xad (i.e. effective seed = xad, not 1.667*xad). Proven on IBM (permno 12490, first non-missing xad at row position 34, fyear 1984, xad=538): golden engine 1996-06 = 101086.40, oracle = 101122.62; recomputing both variants by hand from a_aCompustat reproduces each side exactly (seed-preserved variant 101086.399784 vs recursion-overwrite variant 101122.620392; fyear1996: 73760.38 vs 73767.95 both matching). Difference decays as 0.5^k after the seed year, so all months of affected gvkeys (any firm whose xad history starts after its Compustat history, ~29% of cells: 141,461/489,969) stay beyond rtol=1e-5. Both sides carry 580 identical inf cells (at==0); miss_cand=12 is negligible.
factors.proposed_fix: In _op_brand_invest_signal replicate the script's recursion exactly: initialize brand_capital = zeros (not NaN), set brand_capital[first_pos]=xad/0.6, then run the recursion for i in range(1, len(group)) over ALL rows (so a seed at position>0 is overwritten to tempxad[i]), then mask rows with fyear < FirstNMyear and rows with xad NaN, then divide by at. Note: the oracle behavior is itself a quirk (the paper's seed xad/0.6 only survives for firms whose very first Compustat year has non-missing xad) faithfully inherited from Stata's sequential replace; document it as an oracle artifact being matched deliberately.

factors.evidence: Engine tree = nonfinancial_only(div(sub(sub(revt,cogs),fillna(xsga,0)),at), sic@m_aCompustat) — plain operating profitability. Script CBOperProf.py L118-129 computes the Ball et al. cash-based formula: (revt-cogs-(xsga-xrd)) - d12(rect) - d12(invt) - d12(xpp) + d12(drc+drlt) + d12(ap) + d12(xacc), all 11 inputs fillna(0) (L74-88), scaled by at; then L136-144 nulls where shrcd>11 | mve_c missing | BM=log(ceq/mve_permco) missing | at missing | 6000<=sicCRSP<7000. Proven on IBM 2000-01: engine=0.158409 which equals (revt-cogs-xsga)/at recomputed from m_aCompustat exactly; oracle=0.080023 which equals the full cash-based formula recomputed exactly (2000-06: 0.185542 vs 0.233751, same match). 99% of both-valued cells differ (2,191,974/2,208,062); extra=694,913 are cells the script's shrcd/BM/mve_c/sicCRSP exclusions remove but the engine keeps (engine masks only by m_aCompustat sic, not sicCRSP, and has no shrcd/BM/mve gate).
factors.proposed_fix: Rebuild tree: DIV( ADD( SUB(SUB(fillna(revt,0),fillna(cogs,0)), SUB(fillna(xsga,0),fillna(xrd,0))), NEG(DELTA(fillna(rect,0),12)), NEG(DELTA(fillna(invt,0),12)), NEG(DELTA(fillna(xpp,0),12)), DELTA(ADD(fillna(drc,0),fillna(drlt,0)),12), DELTA(fillna(ap,0),12), DELTA(fillna(xacc,0),12) ), at) then mask: shrcd in (10,11) [SignalMasterTable/monthlyCRSP], mve_c notna, positive ceq/mve_permco (BM=log defined), at notna, and NOT(6000<=sicCRSP<7000) using sicCRSP not Compustat sic. CRITICAL fill-domain detail: the fillna(...,0) must be restricted to months where the permno exists in SignalMasterTable (zero-fill within universe rows only), otherwise DELTA(...,12) manufactures nonzero values across the whole wide grid where the script's lag would be NaN (no SMT row at t-12); e.g. fillna(var,0).where(smt_presence_mask).

factors.evidence: Engine tree = div(cheq@m_QCompustat, atq@m_QCompustat) on the standard m_QCompustat time_avail_m panel. Script Cash.py L67-91 re-times availability from the earnings ANNOUNCEMENT date: time_avail_m = month-start of rdq, each quarterly row expanded to rdq-month +0/+1/+2, overlaps resolved keeping newest rdq; then inner-joins SignalMasterTable on gvkey+month (L109-114) and requires atq>0 (L122). Proven on IBM: quarter with rdq=2000-01-19 (cheq/atq=0.066644) appears in ORACLE at 2000-01..2000-03 but in ENGINE only at 2000-03..2000-05 (engine 2000-01=0.070583, the prior quarter announced 1999-10-20; oracle 2000-01=0.066644) — the engine lags the oracle by ~2 months because standard m_QCompustat time_avail_m is more conservative than rdq-month. Both sides use identical values (cheq/atq matches exactly), pure timing shift explains cells_beyond_tol=1,078,194/2,236,149. extra=693,610: engine broadcasts via the m_aCompustat gvkey->permno map with no SMT inner-join and no atq>0 gate. Oracle also drops singleton gvkey-rdq groups (dup==1 filter quirk, L46-59) — an oracle artifact to replicate.
factors.proposed_fix: Not expressible with LAG on the standard panel (the rdq offset varies per quarter). Add an rdq-timed loader/op for m_QCompustat variables, e.g. RDQ_TIMED(var): dedup gvkey-rdq keeping dup==1 with atq notna (replicating the script's singleton-drop quirk), set month=month(rdq), expand +0/+1/+2 months, keep newest rdq per gvkey-month, broadcast to permnos via SignalMasterTable gvkey join. Then tree = DIV(RDQ_TIMED(cheq), POSITIVE_ONLY(RDQ_TIMED(atq))) masked to the SMT universe. If a new loader op is out of scope, demote to script.

factors.evidence: Engine tree = div(sub(ceq, lag(ceq,12)), lag(ceq,12)) = growth RATE (ratio-1). Script ChEQ.py L53-55: ChEQ = ceq/l12_ceq (ratio LEVEL) and only where BOTH ceq>0 and l12_ceq>0. Proven on IBM 2000-01: engine=-0.019321, oracle=0.980679, ceq=19186, ceq_l12=19564 -> ratio=0.980679, ratio-1=-0.019321; np.allclose confirms engine==ratio-1 and oracle==ratio for all 8 sampled months. Hence 100% of both-valued cells differ (2,974,683/2,974,683) with max_abs~1.000004 (the constant offset of 1). extra=138,285 = missing positivity gate: 6/6 sampled engine-only cells have ceq<=0 or l12_ceq<=0 (e.g. permno 56709 1977-04: engine=-0.68, ceq=-1.17, ceq_l12=-3.662; permno 28740 1969-01: engine=-32.61, ceq_l12=-0.127). Engine also has 60 inf cells (l12=0) vs oracle 0. miss_cand=11,817: script's lag is POSITIONAL shift(12) over gappy m_aCompustat rows (reaches >12 calendar months back for permnos with month gaps) vs engine's calendar shift on the wide grid — a secondary lag-domain mismatch.
factors.proposed_fix: Corrected tree: DIV(POSITIVE_ONLY(ceq), POSITIVE_ONLY(LAG(ceq,12))) — i.e. drop the SUB(...) numerator (ratio, not change) and gate both operands with positive_only (this also kills the inf cells since lag<=0 or lag=0 -> NaN). The residual 11.8k missing-in-engine cells stem from the script's positional-shift-over-gaps quirk (oracle artifact); matching it exactly would require replicating positional lags on the long m_aCompustat rows.

factors.evidence: Firm-level pchcapx is CORRECT in the engine: for IBM 2000-01 both sides imply firm pchcapx=0.028716 recomputed from m_aCompustat capx (capx vs 0.5*(l12+l24)). The divergence is (1) the industry mean: implied 2-digit-SIC mean subtracted by engine = 0.939165 vs oracle = 0.895597 (2000-01), because _op_industry_adjusted_mean (p1_factor_engine.py L887-900) averages over ALL wide-grid permnos with a value (unfiltered monthlyCRSP universe) while the script (ChInvIA.py L35, L92) averages over the SignalMasterTable INNER JOIN m_aCompustat universe (shrcd 10/11/12, exchcd 1/2/3) — a shifted group mean moves EVERY cell in the industry-month, explaining 2,257,121/2,666,062 divergent cells. (2) Division-by-zero is unguarded in the engine's div op (L688-689): golden engine panel contains 689,931 inf cells vs oracle 0 (script L76-79 and L84-89 map denominator==0 to NaN); these infs also poison the grouped mean of every industry-month they appear in, and explain max_abs=Infinity.
factors.proposed_fix: Two changes: (1) guard denominators: pchcapx = COALESCE( DIV(SUB(capx_c, avg), ZERO_TO_NULL(avg)), DIV(SUB(capx_c, LAG(capx_c,12)), ZERO_TO_NULL(LAG(capx_c,12))) ) where capx_c=COALESCE(capx, DELTA(ppent,12)) and avg=DIV(ADD(LAG(capx_c,12),LAG(capx_c,24)),2); additionally make _op_industry_adjusted_mean drop non-finite values before grouping. (2) restrict the industry-mean population to the script's universe: mask pchcapx to SMT membership (shrcd 10/11/12 & exchcd 1/2/3 & m_aCompustat presence) BEFORE the industry_adjusted_mean op, not after.

factors.evidence: Engine tree = numest/LAG(numest,1) - 1: a CONTINUOUS 1-month percent change (golden engine values range -0.97..26.0). Script ChNAnalyst.py L74-88: BINARY indicator vs 3 months ago — 1 iff numest<numest_l3 (l3 notna), 0 iff numest>=numest_l3 (numest notna); oracle uniques are exactly {0,1}. Proven on permno 78908 2005-12: numest=4, numest_l3=6 -> oracle=1; engine=-0.20 (=4/5-1 month-over-month). 2006-06: numest=5>l3=4 -> oracle=0, engine=+0.25. Universe: script filters IBES to fpi=='1' (L33) — the engine's linked-ticker panel loader pivots ALL fpi rows with aggfunc='last' (p1_factor_engine.py L416-431), mixing forecast horizons; script excludes 1987-07..09 (L85-88) and keeps only the bottom 2 monthly size quintiles of mve_c (L92-102) — engine has neither, hence extra=1,782,372 (e.g. IBM permno 12490: oracle non-null count = 0 because IBM is never in the bottom size quintiles, engine has 587 valued months).
factors.proposed_fix: Rebuild as: base numest loaded from IBES_EPS_Unadj restricted to fpi=='1' (dataset variant or load-filter param); indicator = WHERE(numest < LAG(numest,3) & LAG notna, 1, WHERE(numest >= LAG(numest,3) & numest notna, 0, NaN)) — needs an LT_INDICATOR-style op with the script's asymmetric NaN handling; mask months 1987-07..1987-09 (year_filtered-style date-range-exclude op); apply size filter with max monthly mve_c quintile = 2 (existing size_filtered op with min_tercile=None, max_quintile=2, though pd.qcut vs pct-rank tie handling differs slightly). Given three new/modified ops are needed (fpi load filter, asymmetric indicator, date-range exclusion) plus qcut-exact quintiles, demote-to-script is the safer fix; otherwise implement the ops above.

factors.evidence: Engine tree = DIV(DELTA(txtq,12), LAG(atq@m_QCompustat,12)) — QUARTERLY assets denominator. Script ChTax.py L83: ChTax = (txtq - l12_txtq)/l12_at where 'at' is ANNUAL total assets from m_aCompustat (L33-37, merged L50). Proven on IBM 2000-01: engine=0.002873=(867-638)/79719 (atq_l12), oracle=0.002810=(867-638)/81499 (annual at_l12); np.allclose confirms engine==f(atq_l12) and oracle==f(at_l12) across all 8 sampled months. miss_cand=200,492 explained: 6/6 randomly sampled missing-in-engine cells (e.g. permno 14461 1968-11, 22992 2024-06) have atq_l12=NaN while annual at_l12 is present (early/sparse quarterly balance-sheet coverage), so the engine's denominator kills cells the oracle keeps. max_abs=Infinity: both sides carry a few inf cells (engine 14 where atq_l12==0, oracle 34 where l12_at==0 — the script leaves /0 unguarded and save_predictor keeps inf, an oracle artifact). Secondary: engine's gvkey->permno broadcast uses drop_duplicates(gvkey,month) keep-first (L437-443) so multi-permno gvkeys get only one permno, vs script's merge onto per-permno m_aCompustat rows (extra=1,816 / part of miss).
factors.proposed_fix: Corrected tree: DIV(DELTA(txtq@m_QCompustat,12), LAG(at@m_aCompustat,12)) — swap the denominator to annual 'at' from m_aCompustat. Keep /0 unguarded (or map inf->NaN and accept 34 oracle-artifact inf cells as documented divergence). The inner-join universe (both m_aCompustat and m_QCompustat rows present) is naturally enforced by NaN propagation of txtq and at.

factors.evidence: Sampled HAL (permno 23819), 1999-03: engine=0.45, oracle=0.25. Raw IBES_Recommendations for ticker HAL show analyst amaskcd=0 issued TWO recs in 1999-03: anndats 1999-03-09 ireccd=3.0 and 1999-03-30 ireccd=2.0. Engine (p1_factor_engine.py L1471-1472) sorts by anndats before groupby.last() -> picks 2.0 -> firm mean 1.8 -> change = -(1.8-2.25) = +0.45 (matches engine exactly). Script (ChangeInRecommendation.py L31-35) calls groupby(...)['ireccd'].last() WITHOUT any sort, so 'last' is raw parquet file order, which here picks the chronologically EARLIER 3.0 -> mean 2.0 -> +0.25 (matches oracle exactly). The script's intent per its own comment ('last non-missing recommendation') is chronological, so the oracle side is the file-order-dependent quirk; only 55 cells, max_abs 2. Separately, extra=60546 cells: engine maps ticker->permno via IBESCRSPLinkingTable (engine L513-519, L2336) while script inner-merges to SignalMasterTable (script L53-59), which imposes the shrcd 10/11/12 / exchcd 1/2/3 universe.
factors.proposed_fix: Mask engine output to the SignalMasterTable permno-month universe (use SMT's tickerIBES-permno mapping instead of IBESCRSPLinkingTable) to kill the 60,546 extra cells. For the 55 value cells: either accept the engine (chronologically correct, document oracle_artifact) or, to reconcile exactly, drop 'anndats' from the sort in _prepare_recommendation_monthly and preserve raw file order before groupby.last().

factors.evidence: Sampled IBM (12490) 1995-01..1995-08. Oracle 1995-01 = -0.187076 == log(mve_c/mve_c_lag60) - rawBH where rawBH=(idx-idx_lag60)/idx_lag60 over ret lags 0..59 (script L47,55,58 subtracts the RAW buy-and-hold return, not its log); allclose(oracle, script_formula)=True. Engine 1995-01 = -0.245933 == log(mve_permco/mve_permco_lag60) - log(1+compound(ret, lags 1..60, fill 0)); allclose(engine, log-form lags1..60)=True, allclose with lags0..59)=False. So the tree (a) wraps the BH return in LOG(ADD(1,...)) which the script never does, and (b) compounds lags 1..60 instead of 0..59 (the proven systemic extra 1-month lag). 2,560,212 of 2,560,488 both-valued cells differ; max_abs 1949 because raw BH is unbounded while its log is small. Also: params fill_missing:0 zero-fills ret over the whole grid vs script's cumprod-skipna within listing span -> extra=576,557 cells; tree uses monthlyCRSP mve_permco while script uses SMT mve_c -- these differ on 74,572 SMT rows (dual-class permcos; verified SMT mve_c == monthlyCRSP mve_c, != mve_permco).
factors.proposed_fix: Corrected tree: SUB( LOG(DIV(mve_c, LAG(mve_c,60))), COMPOUND_RETURN(ret, lags=[0..59], raw, no +1/log wrapper) ) i.e. subtract the raw compounded return (prod(1+ret_{t-k}, k=0..59) - 1), switch the var from mve_permco to mve_c (monthlyCRSP mve_c), restrict fill_missing=0 to each permno's listed span (missing rets inside span act as 0, outside stay NaN), and mask output to the SignalMasterTable universe.
